# SEV-1 INCIDENT - RELEASE BLOCKER
**Title:** Statements are filing some payments under the wrong kind of transaction, or dropping the payee name
**Owner:** Payments Operations
**Disposition:** Do not ship this release until it is resolved

## What customers reported

Over the past few days support has collected a run of tickets that all share one
shape: the money itself moved fine, but the app files the payment under a category
that does not match what the customer actually did, or shows the wrong name - or
no name at all - beside it. In every case the row that misbehaves carries one very
particular, uncommon form of raw statement text; everyday rows are labeled exactly
as before. The tickets below are anonymized, but the raw narration each customer
pasted is reproduced verbatim, because that raw text is what makes each case
reproducible.

> "I wrote a cheque against my account and the app just lists it as a general
> transfer now - nothing marks it as a cheque anymore. My earlier cheques were
> tagged correctly. The only thing sitting in that row's note is the cheque's own
> number, nothing else around it."

> "My salary came in and the amount is right, but where my employer's name should
> be the app now just prints the word `NACH`. The raw text on that row looks like
> `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` - it used to lift the employer's name off the end
> of that reference, and now it is picking up the wrong piece of it."

> "On some transfers that come in, the sender's name is blank now. Those rows all
> share the same reference layout - a short block of letters, then a long string
> of digits, then the name - for example `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`. The name
> sitting at the end just is not being pulled through anymore; the name column
> comes out empty."

The same batch of complaints also covers two quieter cases that are about the
category rather than the name. The token confirmation charge a bank posts when a
new auto-debit mandate is set up - a small nominal amount, with the note flagging
it as a mandate - is being filed as an ordinary transfer instead of being
recognized as a verification entry. And a refund that came back on a card is
landing as a plain refund for some customers when it should read as a card
reversal; a customer on a different type of account sees the same kind of refund
labeled correctly, so the wrong label appears to depend on the account category.

## Scope of impact

Everyday activity - normal purchases, routine transfers, regular deposits - is
categorized and named correctly, which is precisely why this slipped through QA and
why our monitoring dashboards looked healthy. The breakage is confined to a small
set of unusual transaction forms - among them a note or reference that is exactly
a certain number of digits wide - each one hinging on some exact shape of the raw
row rather than anything about the customer, and each form individually uncommon. But they occur right across the customer base, so they
generate a steady trickle of "why is this labeled wrong" tickets and, more
damaging, they poison the spending-category summaries and payee histories that
several downstream features rely on. That combination is why we are treating it
as ship-blocking rather than a backlog item.

## What we need from engineering

The labeling path is fully deterministic and runs offline - hand it the same
transaction and it reproduces the same wrong answer every time - so each of these
is reproducible on demand and can be pinned down exactly. Get the affected forms
labeling and naming correctly again, and do it without disturbing any transaction
that is already labeled right today. A fix that rescues these cases but nudges the
behavior of ordinary, currently-correct transactions is not acceptable: the pass
condition is simply that the specific problem payments described above come out
right and everything else stays exactly where it is.

# Investigation Report: Transaction Classification & Name Extraction Bugs

## Architecture overview (where classification and name extraction live)

- **Entry point / dispatcher:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/Controller.py`
  - Flask route `categorizeTransaction()` (line 69-70) reads `bank`, `acc_type`, `accountUID`, `accountHolder` from the request (lines 74-77) and dispatches to a per-bank `categorize_<Bank>_transactions(transactions, accountType)` function in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/*.py`.
  - Valid `accountType` values used throughout the app: `"SAVING"`, `"CURRENT"`, `"CREDIT_CARD"` (see Controller lines 94, 106, etc., `Purpose.py:13-16`, `InternalPayment.py:20`, `HDFC.py:124`). Note: singular `SAVING`.
- **Per-bank scripts** each build a `conditions_choices` list evaluated with `np.select(..., default="TRANSFER")` — so any narration that matches no rule falls through to the generic **TRANSFER** bucket. Rule order matters (first match wins).
- **Shared helpers:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/UtilityScripts/AppUtil.py`
  - `sep_by_dash(description, n1, n2)` (line 17) — split on `-`, join slice `[n1:n2]`.
  - `py_extract(description, pat, index)` (line 61) — `str.extract(pat)` then `.get(index)`; **if `index` exceeds the number of capture groups it returns an empty Series**, silently dropping the name.
- **Shared regexes:** `UtilityScripts/RegexConstants.py`, `UtilityScripts/BankRegexConstants.py`.
- **Post-processing:** `UtilityScripts/Purpose.py` (`purpose()`), `UtilityScripts/CleanName.py` (`clean_names()`), `SalaryDetection.py`, `InternalPayment.py`, `PFMCategorization.py`.

The five reported symptoms map to **IDBI**, **IndusInd**, and **Axis** bank scripts.

---

## Case 1 — Digits-only cheque narration classified as TRANSFER

**Files/functions:**
- `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` — `categorize_Indusind_transactions()`, **line 64**:
  ```python
  [transactions.remark.str.contains("^[0-9]{5}$", ...) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT"), "CHEQUE_PAID"],
  ```
  - The regex requires **exactly 5 digits**. Indian cheque numbers are typically **6 digits**, so `123456` fails to match and falls to `default="TRANSFER"` (line 80). I verified: `re.search("^[0-9]{5}$", "123456")` does not match.
  - Every sibling bank uses a range and covers both directions: Axis.py:58-59 `^[0-9]{5,6}$` (DEBIT→CHEQUE_PAID, CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT), PNB.py:60-61 `{5,6}`, BankOfMaharashtra.py:73-74 `{5,6}`, YES.py:52-53 and UCO.py:44-45 `{3,6}`, Kotak.py:65/67 `{3,5}`, RBL.py:49-50 `{1,3}`. IndusInd is the only one with a single exact count **and no CREDIT counterpart** (no CHEQUE_DEPOSIT rule for digits-only remarks) — both smell like a truncated edit of a former `{5,6}` pair.
- Secondary suspect in the same family: `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` lines 55-58 (`categorize_IDBI_transactions()`): the cheque rules only match `"[0-9]{6}-"` (digits **followed by a dash**), `^WTHDRL,CLG`, `CHQ Paid`, `^BY INST`, `CHQ DEP`. A description that is exactly `123456` matches nothing (line 55 requires letters and *no* digits) and falls to TRANSFER. Verified empirically.

Also note the adjacent copy-paste anomaly at Indusind.py:57: the `CHEQUE_DEPOSIT` description rule is gated on `type.eq("DEBIT")` (should be CREDIT), making it dead/wrong.

## Case 2 — `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` yields "NACH" instead of the employer name

**File/function:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` — `categorize_IDBI_transactions()`, partyName block, **line 83**:
```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("^ACH-BD-NACH", ...), sep_by_dash(transactions.description, 2, 3)],
```
- `sep_by_dash(d,2,3)` splits `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` into `[ACH, BD, NACH, ACME INDUSTRIES]` and takes token index 2 → **"NACH"**. The employer name is token 3, so the indices must be `(3, 4)`. Verified: `(2,3)` → `'NACH'`, `(3,4)` → `'ACME INDUSTRIES'`.
- Line 84 (`^ACH-BD-` → `(2,3)`) is correct for the 3-token form `ACH-BD-<NAME>`; line 83 exists precisely to special-case the extra `NACH` token, so its identical `(2,3)` index is clearly a regression (an intentional special case that is now a no-op duplicate of the general rule).
- Compare the correct HDFC analog: `HDFC.py:169` — `^ACH D- BD-NACH-` uses `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)`.

## Case 3 — `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR`: name at end not extracted

**File/function:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/IDBI.py` — `categorize_IDBI_transactions()`, **line 110**:
```python
[transactions.description.str.contains("^[A-Z]{5}[0-9]{10,}", ...),
 py_extract(transactions.description, pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)],
```
- The pattern `"[0-9]{10,} (.*)"` has **only one capture group** (index 0). Passing `index=1` makes `py_extract()` (AppUtil.py:61-66) hit its `res is None` branch and return `pd.Series("")` — the name is silently dropped for *every* row matching this shape. Verified: `index=1` → `''`, `index=0` → `'RAVI KUMAR'`.
- Fix: `index=0` (matching e.g. IDBI.py lines 120-121 which correctly use `index=0`).

## Case 4 — Mandate token confirmation charge filed as TRANSFER instead of ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION

**File/function:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Axis.py` — `categorize_Axis_transactions()`, **line 25**:
```python
[transactions.amount.eq(1) & transactions.description.str.contains("MANDATE|Mandate", ...), "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
```
- Compare the sibling implementation in `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` (structurally near-identical script), lines 29-31:
  ```python
  [... BANK_VER ... & transactions.amount.isin([1,-1]) , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
  [transactions.amount.eq(2) & ...contains("MANDATE|Mandate")... , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],   # Rs 2 mandate token
  [transactions.amount.eq(1) & transactions.type.eq("DEBIT") , "ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION"],
  ```
  The design there is: generic ₹1 penny-drop rules **plus** a dedicated **₹2 mandate-token** rule. In Axis.py the mandate rule's amount gate is `eq(1)`, which is redundant (₹1 is already covered by line 24 `BANK_VER & isin([1,-1])` and line 26 `amount 1 & CREDIT`) and it means a **₹2 debit whose narration flags "MANDATE"** matches nothing (Axis's only other mandate rule, line 28 `MNDTVRFCHGS` → AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES, requires that exact code) and falls through to `default="TRANSFER"` (line 76). Strong indication the gate was regressed from `eq(2)`/`isin([1,2])` to `eq(1)`.
- Related mandate-charge rules for reference: Indusind.py:33, Axis.py:28, PNB.py:14, Syndicate.py:34, Federal.py:21, Canara.py:44, BOI.py:21 (all → `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES`); enum `AUTO_MANDATE_CHARGES` in `TransactionCategoryEnums.py:84`, `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION` at line 83.

## Case 5 — Card refund labeled REFUND instead of CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL, depending on account type

**File/function:** `/app/categorizationapp/categorizationapp/BankScripts/Indusind.py` — `categorize_Indusind_transactions()`, **lines 26-27**:
```python
[ ...("\\bPOS TXN")... & type.eq("CREDIT") & amount.ge(10) & (accountType=="SAVINGS"), "CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL"],
[ ...("\\bPOS TXN")... & type.eq("CREDIT")                & (accountType=="SAVING") , "REFUND"],
```
- The rest of the entire codebase compares against the singular **`"SAVING"`** (Controller.py lines 106/130/..., Purpose.py:13-16, InternalPayment.py:20, HDFC.py:124, ICICI.py:105/113, SBI.py:156 — confirmed by exhaustive grep; Indusind.py:26 is the *only* occurrence of `"SAVINGS"`). Since `acc_type` is passed as `"SAVING"`, line 26 is **unreachable dead code**, and every POS-TXN credit ≥ ₹10 on a savings account falls to line 27 → plain **REFUND** instead of **CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL**.
- For comparison, the same POS-TXN-credit rule in `BankOfMaharashtra.py:31` has no accountType gate and correctly yields CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL. `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` enum: `TransactionCategoryEnums.py:94`. Other banks' card-reversal rules: SBI.py:16, IDFC.py:15, ICICI.py:22-23, HDFC.py:21, BOB.py:19, Canara.py:13, PNB.py:21, IDBI.py:19, etc.
- Also related: Indusind.py:95 uses `accountType=="CURRENT"` for `CARD_RECEIPTS` subcategory (correct constant), reinforcing that `"SAVINGS"` on line 26 is the typo.

---

## Git history

- The repo has **exactly one commit**: `fc21c7f "import codebase"` (author `t <t@t>`, dated 2026-07-15). `git status` clean, no stashes, no dangling objects (`git fsck` clean), reflog shows only the initial commit. So there is **no in-repo diff trail for the regression** — the bugs were baked into the imported snapshot. `/app/.git/opencode` is a 40-byte file containing just the HEAD SHA (tool metadata, not code).
- Evidence of "recent regression" therefore has to come from internal inconsistency, which is strong:
  1. IDBI.py:83 special-case rule that is a **no-op duplicate** of the general rule below it (indices `(2,3)` where only `(3,4)` gives the rule a purpose).
  2. IDBI.py:110 `index=1` on a **one-group regex** (guaranteed-empty extraction; neighbors use `index=0`).
  3. Indusind.py:26 `"SAVINGS"` — the sole plural spelling in the codebase, making the rule dead.
  4. Indusind.py:64 `^[0-9]{5}$` vs. the `{5,6}` / `{3,6}` ranges and DEBIT+CREDIT pairs used by every peer bank.
  5. Axis.py:25 `amount.eq(1)` mandate gate that is redundant given lines 24/26, vs. the ₹2 gate in the sibling Indusind.py:30.

## How tests are run

- **There is no test suite in this repository.** No `tests/` directory, no `test_*.py`/`*_test.py` files, no pytest/tox/CI config, no `setup.cfg`/`pyproject.toml`, no Makefile (verified via glob over the whole tree). `setup.py` declares only runtime deps (Flask 1.1.2, pandas 1.2.4, fuzzywuzzy, gunicorn, scikit-learn, etc.) and no `tests_require`.
- The only way to exercise the code today is to run the service and POST to it:
  - Docker: `Dockerfile` → `pip3 install -e .` inside `/transaction-enrichment-python/categorizationapp`, then `gunicorn -w 4 --timeout 0 -b 0.0.0.0:9898 categorizationapp:app` (port 9898).
  - Locally: `pip install -e /app/categorizationapp` then run the Flask app (`categorizationapp/__init__.py` creates `app`; dev run on port 9898).
  - Endpoints: `POST /categorizeTransaction` with `{bank, acc_type, accountUID, accountHolder, transactions[], isPFMEnabled}` (Controller.py:69) and `POST /recurrentTransactions` (Controller.py:55). Repro payloads would use `bank="IDBI"`, `bank="INDUSIND"` (see Controller dispatch strings), `acc_type="SAVING"`, and transactions carrying `description`, `remark`, `type`, `amount`, `balanceAfterTransaction`.

## Suggested fixes (summary)

| # | File:Line | Current | Fix |
|---|-----------|---------|-----|
| 1 | Indusind.py:64 (and missing CREDIT twin) | `^[0-9]{5}$` DEBIT only | `^[0-9]{5,6}$`, add CREDIT→CHEQUE_DEPOSIT rule (mirror Axis.py:58-59); optionally also cover digits-only descriptions in IDBI.py:55-58 |
| 2 | IDBI.py:83 | `sep_by_dash(...,2,3)` | `sep_by_dash(...,3,4)` |
| 3 | IDBI.py:110 | `py_extract(..., pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` | `index=0` |
| 4 | Axis.py:25 | `amount.eq(1) & MANDATE` | `amount.eq(2)` (or `isin([1,2])`) & MANDATE, per Indusind.py:30 |
| 5 | Indusind.py:26 | `accountType=="SAVINGS"` | `accountType=="SAVING"` |

Resolved. Five one-line fixes across three bank scripts, each mapped to a reported symptom:

## Root causes and fixes

| Ticket | File:Line | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| Cheque filed as transfer | `BankScripts/Indusind.py:64` | Remark regex `^[0-9]{5}$` matched only 5-digit cheque numbers; standard 6-digit numbers fell to the `TRANSFER` default (every peer bank uses a range, e.g. Axis.py:58 `{5,6}`) | `^[0-9]{5,6}$` |
| Salary shows "NACH" instead of employer | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:83` | `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` split on `-` and took token 2 (`NACH`) instead of token 3 (the name); rule was an inert duplicate of the general `^ACH-BD-` rule below it | pattern anchored to `^ACH-BD-NACH-`, indices `(3,4)` |
| Sender name blank on `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` rows | `BankScripts/IDBI.py:110` | `py_extract(pat="[0-9]{10,} (.*)", index=1)` — the pattern has only one capture group (index 0), so `index=1` silently returned `""` for every matching row | `index=0` |
| ₹2 mandate token filed as transfer | `BankScripts/Axis.py:25` | Mandate rule gated on `amount.eq(1)`, making it redundant with the ₹1 rules around it; the ₹2 token debit matched nothing (sibling Indusind.py:30 uses `eq(2)`) | `amount.isin([1,2])` — keeps ₹1 behavior intact, rescues ₹2 |
| Card refund not labeled card reversal on savings accounts | `BankScripts/Indusind.py:26` | `accountType=="SAVINGS"` — the only plural spelling in the codebase (Controller passes `"SAVING"`), so the `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL` rule was dead and all POS-credit refunds fell to the plain `REFUND` rule | `"SAVING"` |

## Verification

- **Repro-first:** all five wrong outputs reproduced exactly as described before any edit; all five come out correct after (`123456` → `CHEQUE_PAID`, `ACH-BD-NACH-ACME INDUSTRIES` → partyName `Acme Industries`, `GBHDL0123456789 RAVI KUMAR` → `Ravi Kumar`, ₹2 mandate → `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION`, POS credit ≥₹10 on SAVING → `CARD_PAYMENT_REVERSAL`).
- **No collateral change:** a 146-row corpus of ordinary and edge-case narrations (UPI/NEFT/RTGS/POS/ATM/interest/cheque/verification, both SAVING and CURRENT) was run against the pristine tree (via a git worktree at the original commit) and the fixed tree; the diff shows changes **only** on the exact reported bug shapes. Deliberate guard rows — 5- and 7-digit remarks, credit-side remarks, 3-token `ACH-BD-NACH…` glued names, the no-space `GBHDL…` variant, ₹1 mandates, large mandate charges, CURRENT-account POS credits — are byte-identical.
- **End-to-end:** the full Flask `/categorizeTransaction` pipeline (categorize → purpose → clean_names → internal payment → salary detection) was exercised via the test client for all three banks; the mandate row even picks up the correct cleaned party name (`HDFC Mutual Fund`) downstream.

Note: the repo has no test suite, so the corpus diff harness lives in `/tmp/opencode/` (`repro.py`, `regress.py`, `e2e.py`) if you want to fold it into CI. Changes are uncommitted, ready for your review.
